name: GitHub Actions OIDC Federation to AWS/GCP
description: Attacker abuses GitHub Actions OIDC token to assume AWS IAM role via STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, pivoting from CI/CD to cloud infrastructure without static credentials
real_world_relevance: CircleCI breach (2023), GitHub Actions OIDC misconfiguration allowing arbitrary repositories to assume production AWS roles, Codecov supply chain attack leveraging CI tokens

techniques.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token

attack_flow.description: Attacker extracts GitHub Actions OIDC token from CI/CD runner environment and exchanges it for cloud provider credentials via STS federation
diagram: 1. Attacker compromises CI/CD runner or injects malicious workflow step
3. Request OIDC token from GitHub's token endpoint
4. Exchange OIDC token for AWS credentials via STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
5. Use cloud credentials to enumerate and access production resources

phases.description: Discover OIDC-related environment variables in the runner

expected_wazuh_alerts.description: NHI: OIDC token exchange via STS federation endpoint
NHI: GitHub Actions OIDC federation to cloud provider - CI/CD to cloud pivot

immediate: Revoke any cloud credentials obtained via compromised OIDC tokens
Audit AWS IAM role trust policies for overly permissive OIDC conditions
Review GitHub Actions workflow logs for unauthorized token requests
long_term: Restrict IAM role trust policies to specific repositories and branches using sub claim conditions
Implement audience restrictions on OIDC federation trust policies
Enable CloudTrail logging for all AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity calls
Use GitHub environment protection rules to limit OIDC token issuance
